subject: Ephemeral BYO key gate and remote attestation review
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <agomez@northbridgetech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Ephemeral BYO key gate and remote attestation review

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for walking through the private deployment constraints. Per our call, I put together a short proposal for the ephemeral BYO key gate we discussed (see attached slides + attestation diagram). High-level:

- Customer-owned key material (BYOK) is wrapped by the on-prem HSM; Redwood runtime keeps only wrapped blobs and ephemeral KEKs for the process lifetime.
- Remote attestation occurs at node boot to verify the HSM firmware/TPM PCRs before unsealing.
- Rotation: customer rotates root keys in their KMS/HSM on their cadence; Redwood supports rewrap APIs and automated rekey flows with an operator-driven confirmation step.

Open items I'd like to confirm with you and your infra team:
1) Acceptable network egress patterns for attestation (mTLS to Redwood attestation endpoints vs. S3-signed uploads).
2) Whether your SOC/controls require us to provide a nonce-based challenge for attestation or if a signed quote is sufficient.
3) Emergency recovery / operator-access protocol — do you want us to build a threshold-unseal path with an out-of-band approval?

Proposed next steps: review attachments, accept the flow or mark changes in the Drive link, and we schedule a 30-min runbook choreograph next week.

Attachments: kb-ephemeral-byok-slides.pdf, attestation-flow-diagram.png, vpc-egress-policy-draft.yaml

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
From: Alex Gomez <agomez@northbridgetech.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Northbridge Infra Team <infra-eng@northbridgetech.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ephemeral BYO key gate and remote attestation review

Kimberly —

Thanks for the write-up and the diagrams, they help a lot. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we circulate to our security ops team:

- Attestation channel: our policy prefers pushing quotes to our internal attestation collector (HTTPS, mTLS, port 443). Can your attestation agent POST the quote rather than Redwood pulling it?
- Nonce handling: we prefer a nonce-challenge flow tied to our session broker to avoid replay risk. Is that compatible with the rewrap API?
- Operator approval: we cannot allow a single human unseal. If you propose an operator-driven confirmation, it must be a 3-of-5 quorum through our KMS operator console.

Also, does the runtime ever store plaintext key material longer than the ephemeral KEK lifetime? Our auditors will ask.

Happy to do the runbook session next Tue; can you share preferred times?

— Alex
Alex Gomez
Principal Infra Engineer | Northbridge Technologies
agomez@northbridgetech.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <agomez@northbridgetech.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Ephemeral BYO key gate and remote attestation review

Alex —

Great questions. Short answers:

- Attestation POST: yes, our on-prem agent supports pushing signed attestation quotes to a customer-configured endpoint (mTLS). We'll include an example mTLS config in the Drive.
- Nonce-challenge: supported. The rewrap API accepts a nonce bound to the session; we can mirror your broker semantics so the quote must include the broker nonce.
- Operator quorum: we support threshold unseal (e.g., 3-of-5) using customer-side HSM key shares — the unseal action requires the configured quorum and an operator audit token. We'll document the audit trail and provide webhook hooks for your audit system.
- Plaintext storage: runtime never persists unwrapped keying material to disk. KEKs live in RAM for the minimal time required to finish the handshake and are zeroed. We also run an attestation-backed enclave process; if the enclave cannot attest, the unseal path is refused.

I'll update the attachments to include the mTLS example and a short runbook checklist. Proposed times for the runbook practice: Wed 14 Jan 10:30–11:00 PT or Tue 20 Jan 09:00–09:30 PT. Which works for you?

Regards,
Kimberly
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Ephemeral BYO key gate and remote attestation review

Folks —

Couple notes for the runbook we should prep before the session with Northbridge:

- Prepare a scriptable demo that shows: node starts -> TPM attests -> agent posts quote -> customer endpoint verifies -> operator awaits quorum -> rewrap completes. Keep the KMS API calls stubbed to avoid leaking any production endpoints.
- Add a troubleshooting appendix showing common failures (cert mismatch on mTLS, stale nonce, missing PCRs) and remediation commands.
- Confirm how we surface token-level billing for rewrap operations (they asked earlier about cost attribution).

Kimberly — can you add the demo steps to the Drive doc? Hiro — please add the PCR list we check on boot and the minimum firmware versions we support.

Vivek
VP Product Operations | Redwood Inference

- We'll prepare the operator roster for the 3-of-5 quorum and share the list with you (will require a short ATO checklist).
- Please send the demo script and troubleshooting appendix early Thursday so we can review before the runbook practice.

Let's lock Wed 14 Jan 10:30–11:00 PT for the runbook session — I appreciate you squeezing this in at short notice.

Best,
Alex
